accepted_interpretation.source_support: The authors state that finite verification of RH over a range amounts to separating zeros of the real-valued Z(t), equivalently finding sufficiently many sign changes. Their programs modify the Rosser-Lehmer Gram-block method. Brent required about 1.41 Z evaluations per separated zero, while the Lune-Riele-Winter strategy reduced this to about 1.21 and later 1.185; statistics imply a floor near 1.135 for any program evaluating every Gram point in the cited range. About 98 percent of runtime was Z evaluation, motivating a refined search strategy for blocks of length at least two.
